noticias.titular: What to watch during MLB's final day of the 2026 season
noticias.texto: There's still much to play for entering the final day of the regular season. We have your guide to the last few games of baseball before October.

noticias.titular: Padres secure home field for wild-card rematch with Cubs
noticias.texto: The Padres beat the Diamondbacks 10-7 to wrap up the No. 4 seed in the NL playoffs. They will host every game in a best-of-three wild-card series against the fifth-seeded Cubs.

noticias.titular: Rangers' quest for AL West title, .500 record down to last day
noticias.texto: The Texas Rangers' quest for an AL West title -- and a .500 record -- will go down to the final day of the regular season.

noticias.titular: Guardians clinch AL Central title, No. 2 seed in playoffs
noticias.texto: Six games behind the White Sox in mid-August, the Guardians clinched their third straight AL Central crown with an 11-5 win over the Royals and will have a first-round bye in the playoffs.

noticias.titular: Rays starter Griffin Jax OK after taking line drive off back
noticias.texto: Rays starter Griffin Jax took a line drive from Philadelphia's Trea Turner off his lower back and left the game after three innings Saturday night.

noticias.titular: Pirates' Kirby Yates retires after 12 MLB seasons, 1st start
noticias.texto: Two-time All-Star reliever Kirby Yates said he is retiring after making his first start Saturday in a 12-year big league career.

noticias.titular: Season over for Dodgers' Blake Treinen after shoulder injury
noticias.texto: Dodgers right-hander Blake Treinen suffered a season-ending shoulder shoulder while warming up in the bullpen late in a 4-3 win Saturday over the Giants.

noticias.titular: Brewers' Yelich named first captain in franchise history
noticias.texto: With franchise legend Robin Yount's approval, Christian Yelich was named the first captain in Brewers history Saturday.

noticias.titular: Phillies turn to Wheeler to right ship, get them in playoffs
noticias.texto: Through all the final-week hardships for the Phillies -- a four-game losing streak, a catcher in an 0-for-34 funk, a punchless offense, a desperate gamble on Aaron Nola -- they are taking solace in one certainty about the final game: win and they're in.
